name: PASTIS
description: Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme Series (PASTIS), the first open-access dataset for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on Satellite Image Time Series (SITS), with over 2 billion annotated pixels covering over 4000 km2. The dataset is comprised of 2,433 sequences of multi-spectral images of shape 10×128×128, with each sequence containing between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019. Each pixel is associated with a semantic label from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class, and each non-background pixel has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index. In total, 124,422 parcels are individualized, each with their bounding box, pixel-precise mask, and crop type.

creator.name: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot and Loic Landrieu
creator.affiliation: LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN, F-94160 Saint-Mande, France

citeAs: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot and Loic Landrieu. Panoptic Segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series with Convolutional Temporal Attention Networks. ICCV 2021.
rai:dataCollection: The satellite images used in PASTIS were gathered from THEIA using Copernicus data processed by CNES for the Theia data cluster. The SITS are taken from 4 different Sentinel-2 tiles in different regions of the French metropolitan territory covering a wide variety of climates and culture distributions. Each tile spans 100×100km and has a spatial resolution of 10 meter per pixel. Each tile is subdivided in square patches of size 1.28×1.28km (128×128 pixels at 10m/pixel), for a total of around 24,000 patches. 2,433 patches (approximately 10% of all available patches) were selected, favoring patches with rare crop types in order to decrease the otherwise extreme class imbalance of the dataset.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Depending on their location, patches are observed a different number of times and at different intervals. This is a result of both the orbit schedule of Sentinel-2 and the policy of Sentinel data providers not to process tile observations identified as covered by clouds for more than 90% of the tile's surface. The proposed SITS are constituted of 33 to 61 acquisitions. Even after the automatic filtering of predominantly cloudy acquisitions, some patches are still partially or completely obstructed by cloud cover. The authors estimate that close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The satellite images were gathered from THEIA using Copernicus Sentinel-2 data. The annotations were taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS).
rai:dataImputationProtocol: All-zeroes images are appended at the end of shorter sequences to match the length of the longer sequence in the batch to facilitate handling of batches by the GPU. A padding mask is retained to prevent the spatial and temporal encoding of padded values, and to exclude these padded values from temporal averages.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The temporal sampling of the sequences in PASTIS is irregular. The authors decided to leave the SITS as is to correspond to the real world setting. The data providers automatically filter tile observations identified as covered by clouds for more than 90% of the tile's surface.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of the Sentinel-2 satellite, after atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel. All bands except the atmospheric bands B01, B09, and B10 were selected. The parcels' extents are cropped along the extent of their 128×128 patch, and the bounding boxes are modified accordingly. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of the patch are annotated with the void label.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All annotations are taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS). The FLPIS allows retrieval of the pixel-precise borders of each parcel and bounding boxes for each parcel. Each parcel is associated with a centerpoint with integer coordinates, a bounding box of size, a binary instance mask, and a class. The FLPIS uses a 73 class breakdown for crop types. Classes with at least 400 parcels and with samples in at least 2 of the 4 Sentinel-2 tiles were selected, leading to an 18-classes nomenclature. Parcels belonging to classes not in the 18-classes nomenclature are annotated with the void label. Pixels which are not within the extent of any declared parcel are annotated with the background 'stuff' label.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each pixel is associated with a semantic label and, for non-background pixels, an instance label. Each parcel has one annotation including bounding box, pixel-precise mask, and crop type.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is split into 5 folds for cross-validation. The official 5-fold cross-validation scheme is provided. Each fold is constituted of patches taken from all four Sentinel tiles with comparable class distributions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Remote monitoring of the surface and nature of agricultural parcels is necessary for a fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (approximately 50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and in the US, respectively) and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected. More generally, the automated analysis of SITS represents a significant interest for a wide range of applications, such as surveying urban development and deforestation.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes. The 2,433 selected patches favor patches with rare crop types in order to decrease the otherwise extreme class imbalance of the dataset. The dataset spans four different regions of France with diverse climates and crop distributions, covering almost 1% of the French Metropolitan territory.
rai:dataLimitations: The temporal sampling of the sequences is irregular due to the orbit schedule of Sentinel-2 and automatic filtering of acquisitions with extensive cloud cover. Close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover. The dataset is limited to French agricultural parcels and may not generalize to other geographic regions or agricultural practices. Thin or visually fragmented parcels are not always recovered correctly. The dataset covers only one year of observations (September 2018 to November 2019).
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on Satellite Image Time Series. It can be used for semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and panoptic segmentation tasks. The dataset allows for 5-fold cross-validation. Geo-referencing metadata of the patches and parcels is included, allowing for the constitution of geographically consistent folds to evaluate spatial generalization.
